title: Tsar Cannon

groundCutout.basis: Only the occupied main stone platform and the complete small ball-contact bed cut terrain. Both masks have closed visible tops; no empty fragment rectangle or surrounding paving flattening.

terrainReference.basis: One host terrain sample at the exact named Tsar Cannon point establishes a common platform/ball-display datum across tiles; not a surveyed paving level.

note: Complete individual Tsar Cannon display: long patinated bronze barrel with genuinely open deep bore and closed breech, thick ringed muzzle, cast bands, paired trunnions and side lifting lugs. Complete dark cast-metal carriage with both large open-spoked wheels, hubs/axle, paired stepped cheeks and crossmembers, rear trail and small support roller, plus an original faceted front casting and geometric scroll/rosette relief. Low stone platform and four separate displayed cannonballs on their small occupied contact bed. Original abstract geometry replaces portraits, arms, lion faces, inscriptions and plaque text. Surrounding trees, chains/bollards, paths, churches, palaces and all native buildings stay independent; no functioning weapon or navigable interior is asserted. Retained Wikidata length5.34m sets the barrel from Z=-2.70 to+2.64. Approximate0.89m bore diameter, outer profile, very slight upward barrel pitch, carriage/wheel proportions, closed internal chamber, original relief,0.36m platform and0.14m ball-contact bed are ordinary-picture medium-fi interpretations, not a casting survey. Both large wheel bottoms and the rear support meet the platform top. A single host terrain sample at the current named point gives common Y=0; standard field144.546875m. The fixture only shifts its vertical reference; raw heights and PNG are unchanged. Native grade varies by about0.30m across the platform. +X north across the axle; +Z east along the barrel toward the muzzle and displayed balls; +Y up. Ordinary-picture approximation, not a surveyed bearing. Preview uses the host terrain sample at the authored base; ground slope, facade azimuth and final site fit remain review items.
